title: Redis — Debug & Runbook

panels.title: Redis errors (window)
panels.description: Redis log lines that look like errors or failures in the selected time range.

targets.rawSql: SELECT count() AS value FROM default.logs WHERE service LIKE 'redis%' AND $__timeFilter(timestamp) AND (level IN ('ERROR','FATAL') OR message ILIKE '%error%' OR message ILIKE '%fail%' OR message ILIKE '%down%' OR message ILIKE '%lost%')

panels.title: Pod restarts (1h)
panels.description: Container restarts for the master and replica in the last hour.

panels.title: Memory used
panels.description: Working set held by the Redis containers (master + replica).

panels.title: CPU used (cores)
panels.description: Cores actually used by Redis right now (master + replica).

panels.title: Redis logs — $service | $search
panels.description: All Redis master/replica log lines. Narrow with the Service and Search variables at the top.

targets.rawSql: SELECT timestamp, message, service, level FROM default.logs WHERE service LIKE '$service' AND message ILIKE '%${search}%' AND $__timeFilter(timestamp) ORDER BY timestamp DESC LIMIT 500

panels.title: Errors, warnings and failures
panels.description: Anything that should not be happening. Empty is good.

targets.rawSql: SELECT timestamp, message, service, level FROM default.logs WHERE service LIKE '$service' AND (level IN ('ERROR','FATAL','WARN') OR message ILIKE '%error%' OR message ILIKE '%fail%' OR message ILIKE '%down%' OR message ILIKE '%lost%' OR message ILIKE '%denied%') AND $__timeFilter(timestamp) ORDER BY timestamp DESC LIMIT 500

panels.title: Replication & sync
panels.description: Master/replica handshake and resync events. Look for repeated 'MASTER <-> REPLICA sync started' lines — they mean flapping.

targets.rawSql: SELECT timestamp, message, service, level FROM default.logs WHERE service LIKE '$service' AND (message ILIKE '%replic%' OR message ILIKE '%sync%' OR message ILIKE '%master%' OR message ILIKE '%slave%' OR message ILIKE '%ready to accept%' OR message ILIKE '%partial resync%') AND $__timeFilter(timestamp) ORDER BY timestamp DESC LIMIT 500

panels.title: CPU usage % by pod
panels.description: Percentage of each Redis pod's CPU limit in use. Redis is single-threaded: sustained 100% throttles every command.

panels.title: Memory usage % by pod
panels.description: Percentage of each Redis pod's memory limit held. Nearing 100% means evictions or an OOM kill is next.

panels.title: Persistence & background saves
panels.description: RDB snapshots and AOF rewrites. A save that starts but never terminates points at disk I/O.

targets.rawSql: SELECT timestamp, message, service, level FROM default.logs WHERE service LIKE '$service' AND (message ILIKE '%saving%' OR message ILIKE '%saved%' OR message ILIKE '%RDB%' OR message ILIKE '%fork%' OR message ILIKE '%AOF%' OR message ILIKE '%bgrewrite%') AND $__timeFilter(timestamp) ORDER BY timestamp DESC LIMIT 500

options.content:
## Copy/paste runbook

Run these from the repo root. `REDIS_PW` comes from `.env`; never paste the
password into a ticket or a Grafana panel.

```bash
export REDIS_PW=$(sed -n 's/^REDIS_PASSWORD=//p' .env)
MASTER=$(kubectl -n pfa get pod -l app=redis -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}')
REPLICA=$(kubectl -n pfa get pod -l app=redis-replica -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}')
CLI="redis-cli -a $REDIS_PW --no-auth-warning"
```

### 1. Is it alive?

```bash
kubectl -n pfa exec $MASTER  -- $CLI ping                 # PONG
kubectl -n pfa exec $REPLICA -- $CLI ping
kubectl -n pfa exec $MASTER  -- $CLI info server | grep -E 'redis_version|uptime_in_seconds|process_id'
kubectl -n pfa exec $MASTER  -- $CLI info keyspace        # db0:keys=…,expires=…,avg_ttl=…
kubectl -n pfa exec $MASTER  -- $CLI dbsize
```

### 2. Replication (why reads are stale)

```bash
kubectl -n pfa exec $MASTER  -- $CLI info replication     # role:master, connected_slaves
kubectl -n pfa exec $REPLICA -- $CLI info replication     # role:slave, master_link_status:up
```

Watch `master_link_status` (must be `up`), `master_last_io_seconds_ago`
(should be < 10) and compare `slave_repl_offset` to the master's
`master_repl_offset`.

### 3. Memory, eviction and hit rate

```bash
kubectl -n pfa exec $MASTER -- $CLI info memory \
  | grep -E 'used_memory_human|maxmemory_human|maxmemory_policy|mem_fragmentation_ratio'
kubectl -n pfa exec $MASTER -- $CLI info stats \
  | grep -E 'keyspace_hits|keyspace_misses|evicted_keys|rejected_connections|expired_keys'
kubectl -n pfa exec $MASTER -- $CLI config get maxmemory-policy
```

`evicted_keys` climbing = the cache is under pressure: raise the limit or
reduce TTLs. A falling hit ratio with a growing `dbsize` usually means stale
cache keys, not a Redis fault.

### 4. Auth caches (auth-service / query-service)

```bash
kubectl -n pfa exec $MASTER -- $CLI --scan --pattern 'refresh_token:*' | head
kubectl -n pfa exec $MASTER -- $CLI --scan --pattern 'user_tokens:*'    | head
kubectl -n pfa exec $MASTER -- $CLI --scan --pattern 'token_blacklist:*'| head
kubectl -n pfa exec $MASTER -- $CLI ttl  'refresh_token:<id>'
kubectl -n pfa exec $MASTER -- $CLI memory usage 'refresh_token:<id>'
```

Prefer `--scan` over `keys '*'`; `keys` blocks the single-threaded server.

### 5. Slow operations and clients

```bash
kubectl -n pfa exec $MASTER -- $CLI slowlog len
kubectl -n pfa exec $MASTER -- $CLI slowlog get 20
kubectl -n pfa exec $MASTER -- $CLI info clients | grep -E 'connected_clients|blocked_clients'
kubectl -n pfa exec $MASTER -- $CLI client list
kubectl -n pfa exec $MASTER -- $CLI latency latest
```

### 6. Live traffic (short burst only)

```bash
kubectl -n pfa exec $MASTER -- $CLI monitor      # Ctrl-C after a few seconds
```

`monitor` adds load and can print secrets — use it for seconds, not minutes.

### 7. Persistence checks

```bash
kubectl -n pfa exec $MASTER -- $CLI info persistence | grep -E 'rdb_last_bgsave_status|aof_last_bgrewrite_status|rdb_changes_since_last_save'
kubectl -n pfa exec $MASTER -- $CLI bgsave      # async; never `save` in prod
```

### Last resort

`FLUSHDB` / `FLUSHALL` delete the auth token caches and every cached
aggregate. Only run after a verified backup, and expect all users to be
logged out.

description: Redis master/replica logs, pod pressure, replication health and copy-paste redis-cli commands. Start here when caching, login tokens or read freshness look wrong.
